hospitals.description: Morgan Stanley Children's Hospital is the Columbia side of NewYork-Presbyterian's children's program, sitting at Broadway and 165th Street in Washington Heights at the top of Manhattan. Its roots go back to Babies Hospital, founded in 1887, and the current building opened in 2003. It is a full quaternary referral center with a large PICU that includes a dedicated cardiac ICU, a level IV NICU, and one of the busiest pediatric ECMO programs in the world. The hospital is the only Level I pediatric trauma center in Manhattan and draws complex cardiac, transplant and neonatal patients from across the region and abroad. The surrounding neighborhood is dense and residential, with the George Washington Bridge and Fort Tryon Park close by.
highlights: Tied with Komansky as the top-ranked children's hospital in New York (U.S. News 2025)
Only Level I pediatric trauma center in Manhattan
Level IV NICU with about 50 beds and a 41-bed PICU including 14 cardiac ICU beds
ELSO Platinum Center of Excellence for pediatric ECMO
Site of the first successful pediatric heart transplant (1984)
ACS Level I Children's Surgery Center and NYS Regional Perinatal Center
hospitals.notes: Wikipedia gives 299 beds in the infobox and 269 in the body; peds_beds left null. NYP STAT transport brings critically ill children in from the region. Posting location is usually NYP Columbia University Irving Medical Center or Morgan Stanley Children's.

hospitals.description: Komansky Children's Hospital is the Weill Cornell half of NewYork-Presbyterian's pediatric program, located inside the Weill Cornell Medical Center campus on York Avenue on the Upper East Side. It cares for patients from birth to about age 20 and runs a pediatric critical care service, a pediatric trauma program and the only pediatric burn unit in the region. Its NICU is housed in the Alexandra Cohen Hospital for Women and Newborns in the David H. Koch Center a block away, which New York State designates as a Regional Perinatal Center. The campus sits along the East River near Rockefeller University and Memorial Sloan Kettering, in one of the densest medical corridors in the country.

hospitals.description: Cohen Children's is Northwell Health's only children's hospital and one of the largest pediatric programs in the New York area, sharing the Long Island Jewish Medical Center campus on the Queens and Nassau line. It opened in 1983 as Schneider Children's Hospital and took its current name in 2010 after a major gift. A 2013 expansion added a dedicated pediatric emergency department, a 24-bed PICU, a surgical unit and pediatric operating rooms. It is an ACS-verified Level I pediatric trauma center and its NICU sits within LIJ's Regional Perinatal Center. The campus is suburban and car friendly, an easy drive from eastern Queens and western Nassau.

hospitals.description: Hassenfeld Children's Hospital is NYU Langone's children's hospital, occupying dedicated floors of the Kimmel Pavilion on the main NYU Langone campus along First Avenue in Kips Bay. The current space opened in 2018 after a $50 million naming gift from the Hassenfeld family, and the hospital serves patients up to 21, with some programs extending to 25. It runs the KiDS Emergency Department, an expanded congenital heart program and a pediatric lung transplant program that performed its first double-lung transplant in 2021. Its NICU sits within NYU Langone's Regional Perinatal Center. The campus is on the East River in Midtown East, a short walk from Bellevue, where NYU faculty also staff the pediatric service.

hospitals.description: The Children's Hospital at Montefiore, known as CHAM, is a ten-story children's hospital attached to Montefiore's Moses campus in the Norwood section of the Bronx. It opened in 2001 as the first major children's hospital built in New York City in decades and serves patients up to 21 from across the Bronx and Westchester. Inside are a 26-bed PICU, a 35-bed AAP level III NICU, a 36-bed pediatric cardiology unit, a 28-bed adolescent unit and a 17-bed pediatric emergency department. The building is known for its space-themed design with NASA artifacts throughout. The neighborhood is residential and close to Mosholu Parkway and the Bronx River.
highlights: Montefiore Health System's only children's hospital
26-bed PICU and 35-bed level III NICU
17-bed pediatric emergency department
Dedicated 36-bed pediatric cardiology unit and 28-bed adolescent unit
Neonatology and pediatric GI nationally ranked (U.S. News 2021)
Opened 2001, academic home of Einstein pediatrics
hospitals.notes: Wikipedia's CHAM article says 193 pediatric beds while the Montefiore article says 106; the larger figure is used. Pediatric trauma goes to nearby Jacobi (Level II pediatric trauma). Montefiore's Weiler (Einstein) campus holds the NYS Regional Perinatal Center designation, so the Weiler NICU may be higher acuity than the level III stated for CHAM.

hospitals.description: Kravis Children's Hospital is the pediatric arm of The Mount Sinai Hospital, the flagship of the Mount Sinai Health System on the Upper East Side at the edge of Central Park and East Harlem. Mount Sinai created one of the first pediatrics departments in an American general hospital in 1878, and Kravis carries that program forward for patients from infancy to 21. It shares the main campus with Mount Sinai's Regional Perinatal Center and its NICU, along with pediatric emergency and critical care services. The hospital is tied with NYU's Hassenfeld as one of the top-ranked children's programs in the state. Central Park, Museum Mile and the 6 train are steps away.

hospitals.description: Maria Fareri Children's Hospital is the children's hospital of Westchester Medical Center, the academic hub of the WMCHealth network on the Grasslands campus in Valhalla. It is the tertiary pediatric referral center for the Hudson Valley, a large region stretching from Westchester north toward the Catskills. The hospital runs a regional level IV NICU, pediatric critical care, pediatric cardiothoracic surgery and a pediatric liver transplant program, and WMCHealth describes it as the only Level I pediatric trauma center in the Hudson Valley. The campus is suburban, next to New York Medical College and the Taconic and Sprain Brook parkways, about 30 minutes north of the Bronx.

hospitals.description: Bellevue is the oldest public hospital in the United States and the flagship of NYC Health + Hospitals, standing on First Avenue in Kips Bay next to the NYU Langone campus. It is a Level I adult and Level II pediatric trauma center and runs a separate pediatric emergency service for patients under 25. New York State designates it a Regional Perinatal Center, so its NICU takes high-risk transfers from other public hospitals. NYU Grossman School of Medicine faculty staff the clinical services, which makes it a major teaching site for NYU pediatrics residents and fellows. The patient population is diverse and largely publicly insured, with a strong safety-net mission.

hospitals.description: Duker Children's Hospital is the 125-bed children's hospital inside Albany Medical Center, the only academic medical center in northeastern New York. More than 140 physicians across about 40 subspecialties care for infants, children and teens referred from a 25-county area that reaches into western New England. The Massry Family Children's Emergency Center opened in 2018, and in 2023 the American College of Surgeons verified Albany Med as a Level I pediatric trauma center, the first in the region and the eighth in New York. Albany Med is also a NYS Regional Perinatal Center. The campus sits in Albany's Pine Hills and New Scotland neighborhoods near Washington Park, with Saratoga, the Berkshires and the Adirondacks within easy reach.

Rochester offers a lower cost of living than downstate with Lake Ontario and the Finger Lakes nearby.

hospitals.description: Buffalo's freestanding children's hospital opened in November 2017 on the Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus, replacing the old Women and Children's Hospital of Buffalo. It opened as John R. Oishei Children's Hospital and was set to take the Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo name in January 2026 after a $50 million gift from Tom Golisano. The 185-bed building includes a 64-bed NICU and adult obstetrics, and it is an ACS-verified Level I pediatric trauma center with a rooftop helipad. It is part of Kaleida Health and the main pediatric teaching hospital for the University at Buffalo. The medical campus sits just north of downtown Buffalo, within walking distance of Allentown and the Elmwood Village.

hospitals.description: Upstate Golisano Children's Hospital is the 71-bed children's hospital built into the East Wing of Upstate University Hospital, SUNY's academic medical center on University Hill in Syracuse. It opened in 2009 and is the pediatric referral center for central New York, with a regional PICU and ACS-verified Level I pediatric trauma care. Upstate University Hospital is the region's only ACS-verified Level I trauma center and earned Magnet designation in 2021. The regional NICU for Syracuse sits next door at Crouse Hospital, which holds the Regional Perinatal Center designation. University Hill is a compact academic district beside Syracuse University, a few minutes from downtown.
